answer: Live cross-examination stops bulk fakes by requiring a live human behind each one. Each epoch a beacon picks 5 percent of identities and sends each a fresh signal question from its recent work, due in ten minutes. Responder rental fails here: one operator cannot cover simultaneous slots, and a pearl detail in each answer, a fact only its worker would know, exposes copied replies and freezes the identity. The k-th fake still needs a k-th paid responder at $15 an hour, so 1,000 fakes cost $15,000 per round, while an honest agent pays nothing extra and keeps its nectar share.
